headings.text: Level 1. Current explicit decision by the creator

blocks.text: Public project: Symphony of Justice | Internal/original name: Symphonia Iustitiae

The World and Lore Index functions as the master navigation and control document for the Symphony of Justice World Bible. Its purpose is not to develop the universe's history exhaustively, but to make it possible to identify:
which documents are part of the World Bible;
what information is currently considered CANON;
which decisions are still under review;
what contradictions exist between historical documents and current decisions;
which areas still lack sufficient information;
which sources support each major decision;
what information may later be used in the video game, Vertical Slice, website, or presentation materials.

The World Bible must function as the project's central source of narrative truth. When a nation, character, event, deity, organization, or world rule appears in different documents, the World Bible must make it possible to determine which version is currently valid.
The project contains several years of documentation, concepts, rewrites, and different versions. For this reason:
The existence of an idea within the historical material does not automatically make it [text missing in source]. When there is a contradiction between earlier material and current decisions:
the old version will not be silently removed;
the historical source will be identified;
the current decision will be documented.
The goal is to preserve the project's creative evolution without allowing earlier versions to create contradictions in production.
When two sources conflict, the following order of priority will be used:
Level 1. Current explicit decision by the creator
Decisions directly confirmed by J. Crow have the highest narrative authority. These decisions must later be transferred into the corresponding World Bible documents.
Once a concept is officially incorporated into the current World and Lore documents and marked as CANON, that version becomes the official production reference.

When a narrative rule has gameplay consequences, it must remain compatible with the current Game Design documents. The current Game Vision already establishes, for example, that the world should be built around different perspectives on what may be considered just, and that learning those perspectives is part of the player's experience.
